sections.h2: Where is the Webster County Clerk, and what does the office do for a seller?
sections.html:
The Clerk works from the Webster County Courthouse at 25 US Highway 41-A South, Dixon, KY 42409, Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. For recordings, call 270-639-7006; vehicle registration has its own line at 270-639-7005, and the fax is 270-639-7029.

Beyond vehicle licensing, voter registration, elections, and marriage licenses, the office records every land record in the county and processes delinquent real estate taxes. A seller deals with it in three situations: when the deed to the buyer is recorded, when an old mortgage needs its release on the record, and when a tax bill has slipped past the Sheriff's April 15 cutoff and landed with the Clerk.

The Clerk's land records page notes that recorded instruments go back to 1786, even though the county itself was formed in 1860.

sections.h2: Can I search Webster County land records online?
sections.html:
Yes, and at no charge. The Clerk put records online on August 1, 2010, and the indexing and back-scanning continue. The site lists what is available to view:

  • Deeds from 1860 (Book 1) to the present, and deeds of partition from 1893 to 2017.
  • Mortgages from 1972 forward and encumbrances from 1974 forward.
  • Plats, all current, with early plats in the two Processioner books (1861 to 1912).
  • Wills and marriage records from 1860 to the present, and all fixture filings.
  • Miscellaneous records from 1939 (Book 20) onward, plus a delinquent tax lookup.

Two searches are worth doing before listing a house. Search your own name to confirm the mortgage shows a recorded release once it is paid. Then look for liens, lis pendens notices, and judgments against you or a prior owner, since an unreleased item found by a title company in the last week can delay a closing.

sections.h2: How must a document be formatted for the Webster County Clerk?
sections.html:
Since January 1, 2020, Kentucky's county clerks have used the Property Records Industry Association formatting standards, and Webster County follows them. A deed that ignores them can be turned back at the counter.

  • 20 lb white paper, 8 1/2 by 11 preferred (8 1/2 by 14 accepted), no watermarks.
  • Print on one side only, with no staples, binding, impression seals, or highlighter.
  • Leave the top 3 inches of page one blank for the recorder's stamp; other margins 1 inch.
  • Black ink preferred with dark blue signatures, 10-point Times New Roman or equivalent, no more than 9 lines per inch.

A title attorney or closing agent normally prepares and files a sale deed, so a seller rarely handles this directly. It matters most for family transfers written from a template.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a document in Webster County?
sections.html:
The Clerk publishes a fee schedule, effective January 1, 2020. A flat charge applies to each document, and $3.00 is added for every page over five.

Webster County Clerk recording fees (clerk's published schedule)

Deed$50.00
Deed of correction$46.00
Mortgage (up to 30 pages)$80.00
Release of mortgage$46.00
Assignment of mortgage$46.00
Affidavit of descent$50.00
Power of attorney$50.00
Plat$50.00
Lis pendens notice$46.00

Will$47.00
Certified copy$5.00

A mortgage with an assignment runs $126.00 for up to 30 pages. Confirm the total with the office before mailing a packet.

sections.h2: What must a deed contain for the Webster County Clerk to accept it?
sections.html:
Kentucky law bars a clerk from lodging a deed that misses the content rules in KRS 382.135 and KRS 382.110. The deed is recorded in the county where the property, or most of it, lies.

  • Full names and mailing addresses of the grantor and grantee.
  • A statement of the full consideration, backed by a sworn, notarized certificate signed by both sides. A gift deed carries a certificate saying so, with the estimated fair cash value.
  • An in-care-of address for the property tax bill for the year of transfer.
  • The source of the grantor's title: the deed book, page, and recording date of the earlier deed, or a plain statement of how and from whom title came by inheritance.

When land passes by will or intestacy, the personal representative files an affidavit with the clerk of each county where it lies, naming who receives each parcel and its estimated value, before closing the estate. A clerk that records a noncompliant deed does not undo the notice effect of the filing, but a title insurer may still raise the defect.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax does a Webster County seller pay at the Clerk?
sections.html:
The grantor owes 50 cents for each $500 of value, rounded up to the next $500, under KRS 142.050. The Clerk computes it from the value stated in the deed, collects it before accepting the deed, and certifies the date and amount on the deed itself. It is collected once per transaction.

A sale at $200,000 is 400 blocks of $500, so the tax is $200. A sale at Webster County's Census median owner-occupied value of $112,900 is 226 blocks, or $113. The Clerk keeps 5 percent for collecting, and the rest goes to the county treasurer every three months for the general fund.

Exemptions include foreclosure deeds and deeds in lieu, transfers between spouses or former spouses in a divorce, partitions, deeds that only confirm or correct an earlier deed, security deeds, and gifts between parent and child or grandparent and grandchild for nominal consideration. If a deed states no price, the tax is figured on the open-market estimate.

sections.h2: Which deadlines and other filings can affect a Webster County sale?
sections.html:
Two filing clocks sit in KRS 382.110. A lender that accepts a deed in lieu of foreclosure must file it with the county clerk within 45 days of signing. A grantee holding a deed from a court-appointed commissioner has five business days from receipt to file it. If you are the seller in either kind of transfer, confirm with the other side that the deed has been recorded before treating the matter as closed.

Other recordings may come up. A recorded mortgage release clears the old loan. A mechanic lien or lis pendens notice must be released or resolved before a clean title can pass. An affidavit of descent documents who inherited a parcel. For help with the Webster County tax side of a sale, the Clerk also receives certificates of delinquency from the Sheriff after April 15, so ask the office for a payoff on any prior-year bill before listing.

Webster County has 4,923 households and a 73.8 percent owner-occupied rate, with a median home value of $112,900 per Census QuickFacts. Homes that need repairs, inherited houses, and properties with liens are common reasons to sell as-is for cash, and the recording steps above are the same for any sale.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Webster County?
faqs.a: Record it with the County Clerk at 25 US Highway 41-A South in Dixon, which is open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. The phone for recordings is 270-639-7006.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Webster County?
faqs.a: A deed is $50.00, plus $3.00 for each page over five, under the Clerk's schedule. A mortgage release is $46.00 and a certified copy is $5.00.

faqs.q: How is the Kentucky transfer tax figured on a Webster County sale?
faqs.a: It is 50 cents per $500 of value, rounded up, charged to the seller. A $200,000 sale produces $200 in tax, collected by the Clerk before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Can I look up Webster County deeds and mortgages for free?
faqs.a: Yes. The Clerk's site offers free online records: deeds back to 1860, mortgages from 1972, plats, wills, and a delinquent tax lookup.

faqs.q: How long does a lender have to record a deed in lieu in Webster County?
faqs.a: Forty-five days after the deed in lieu of foreclosure is signed, under KRS 382.110. A grantee under a commissioner's deed has five business days after receiving it.
